name: Base64 Converter
description: Encode text to base64 and decode it back, with a personal history for signed-in users
backend_requirements: Access control: anyone may encode and decode without saving; require auth for saving conversions and for reading or deleting the conversion history; restrict each user's history to that user; admin endpoints are restricted to the admin account
Encoding takes the text as UTF-8 and produces standard base64 with padding; text may be empty and is at most 100000 characters

Decoding ignores surrounding whitespace and line breaks and accepts missing padding; input that is not valid base64, or that decodes to bytes that are not valid UTF-8, answers 400; encoded input is at most 140000 characters
POST /api/base64/encode and POST /api/base64/decode convert without storing anything

POST /api/conversions converts like the endpoints above (direction encode or decode) and also saves the conversion to the signed-in user's history, storing only the first 200 characters of the input and of the output; it returns the full output
GET /api/conversions returns the signed-in user's active conversions newest first; ?page= and ?page_size= page the result (page_size default 20, at most 100), and total counts all of them
DELETE /api/conversions/:id removes one of the signed-in user's conversions permanently
Deactivated conversions (is_active false) are left out of the owner's history; the admin overview still lists them
Errors answer with a JSON object {"detail": "<message>"}: 400 for invalid input, 401 without a valid token, 403 for a non-admin on admin endpoints, 404 for unknown ids
frontend_requirements: Everyone can use the converter; signed-in users also get a 'Save to history' switch and a history panel, and visitors see a 'Sign in to keep a history' prompt in their place
Sign-in and registration forms that call /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register; keep the token for later requests, show the signed-in username and offer sign-out
Two text areas, input and output, with Encode and Decode buttons; with 'Save to history' on the conversion goes through /api/conversions, otherwise through /api/base64/encode or /api/base64/decode
Decode errors from the API appear next to the input, and the output is cleared
A swap button that moves the output into the input, and a copy button that copies the output to the clipboard and confirms it

History panel: the user's conversions with direction, input and output previews and time, previous/next paging, a delete control per entry, and selecting an entry loads its input preview into the input
admin_requirements: Admin overview: every saved conversion, active or not, with its user and total, active and inactive counts
Toggle a conversion's active status from the overview

api_endpoints.description: Convert and save the conversion to the signed-in user's history
